cme.note: CME first seen to the NW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-11-11T23:24Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap which began at 2026-11-11T12:23Z. The source of this event is field line opening seen originating from Active Region 14565 (N14W86) in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 284 beginning at approx. 2026-11-11T22:55Z. This AR is in close proximity to a large coronal hole, potentially resulting in some deflection.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1.

cme.note: CME first seen to the W part way into the FOV of STEREO A COR2 following a real-time data gap that ended at 2026-11-12T01:53Z. The source may be related to some "flickering" seen beyond the WSW limb in STA EUVI after a real-time data gap ending at 2026-11-12T01:55Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen due to beyond-limb source and single coronagraph view.

cme.note: Faint CME seen to NNW in early SOHO LASCO C2 coronagraph imagery and very faintly in early timestamps of GOES CCOR-1 but completely covered by an evening data gap in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph. Its source is most likely a faint prominence seen erupting on/behind the NNW limb starting at 2026-11-12T21:13Z, as seen to the NNW in GOES SUVI 304. Unfortunately, the source cannot be seen in STEREO A EUV imagery, since it is covered by the above mentioned data gap in STEREO A.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen due to beyond-limb source and single coronagraph view, because of the data gap in STEREO A.

cme.note: CME visible to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery and to the SSE in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The potential source is not clear, but some faint dimming and moving field lines are seen to the far south in SDO AIA 171/193 imagery starting around 2026-11-12T17:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The leading edge of the CME is unclear, so this measurement is more approximate than usual and based on the fastest portion of the CME prior to it leaving the field of view of STEREO A COR2.

cme.note: This CME is faintly visible to the NE in STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The CME is not seen in GOES CCOR-1 due to Earthshine starting 2026-11-13T03:45Z. The potential source may be an eruption with a small region of dimming and post-eruption arcades starting at 2026-11-13T00:21Z as best seen in SDO AIA 193 imagery from Active Region 14575 (S09E50).

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. This measurement only uses one frame of available SOHO LASCO C2 imagery and is primarily based on STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cme.note: CME faintly visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is not clear, but may be some faint field line movement seen to the west in STEREO A COR2 EUV 195 imagery around 2026-11-13T08:00Z. Dimming is also seen to the south of the large coronal hole seen in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery as well. Moving/opening field lines are visible beyond the west limb in SDO AIA 171 in ISWA starting at 2026-11-13T08:27Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

cme.note: A faint messy front seen to the SSW in SOHO LASCO C2 and later in C3 and GOES CCOR-1 as a messy fuzzy half-loop. There is also a much fainter loop seen in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph to the SW, but this loop in STEREO A COR2 seems to be starting much earlier (first seen ~13Z), so it is likely a different event.

A very small CME seen to the SSW in SOHO LASCO C2 and to the SE in STEREO A COR2 coronagraphs, and in early timestamps of C3. The front is not clear in GOES CCOR-1. No source has been found for this CME.

This CME is visible to the south/southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and to the southeast in STEREO A COR2 imagery. There are no clear sources observed on the Earth-facing disk around the time of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cme.note: This CME is visible to the south/southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and to the southeast in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source may be related to a small filament eruption centered near S45W25 as seen in SDO AIA 304 imagery which begins to lift off around 2026-11-14T03:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cme.note: This CME is visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. This event is not seen in STEREO A COR2 imagery due to a data gap starting at 2026-11-14T13:23Z. The source is likely far-sided as there are no corresponding source signatures on the Earth-facing disk around the time of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of -90 degrees due to the far-sided and therefore unknown source location.
